Vision and Values
Our School
Vision and Values
Vision
Our school vision is to ensure that everyone has the 'roots to grow and wings to fly'.
It is inspired by Psalm 1 and Isaiah 40:30-31:
‘They are like trees that grow beside a stream, that bear fruit at the right time, and whose leaves do not dry up. They succeed in everything they do.’
‘Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall; but those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.’
Roots and wings. We need them both. The roots of our community that nurture and help us grow to be the best possible versions of ourselves. The wings of faith that allow us to soar freely into the future.
Values
Our school values, based on Christian teaching, are: Respect, Responsibility, Perseverance, Trust, Teamwork and Creativity. Through these values we strive to develop character and inspire everyone to achieve in a happy, fun and safe environment. This journey is summarised in our school motto: 'Learn, Create, Laugh, Grow'.
Respect: Our school golden rule - 'Do to others as you would have them do to you' (Matthew 7.12) helps us all to value others, places and opinions that may be different to our own.
Responsibility: “Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might” (Eccles 9:10) Our pupils are given a range of responsibilities to help them grow and become more independent. For example representing the school in sporting festivals, taking a lead as part of the school or eco-council or being buddies with children from a younger class.
Perseverance: 'I can do all things through Him who strengthens me' (Philippians 4.13) reminds us to do the right thing and keep going when we face the challenges in our lives.
Trust: 'My God is my strength in whom I trust' (Psalm 18.2) helps us to learn about being trustworthy and being there for our friends when they need us.
Teamwork: 'Serve one another in love' (Galatians 5.13). Closely related to service, teamwork teaches us how to be there for others, giving without expecting something in return and living for others.
Creativity: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth' (Genesis 1.1). All life is a 'gift' and we have a creative spirit within each of us to help us learn to value and explore, celebrate and enjoy our world, with all its mystery and diversity.
Our vision and values are at the core of everything we do. We support, encourage and nurture everyone to aspire to be the best possible versions of themselves so that they realise their full potential; both in their learning and in their relationships.
Aims
As a Church of England primary school we aim to make sure that:
Achievement is celebrated whenever possible.
Everyone values and respects each other.

Oakwell Breakfast and After-School Club
Oakwell Breakfast and After-School Club
Breakfast and After-School Club
Oakwell Breakfast and After-School Club is led by Mrs Donna Waldron and Emma Waldron at Crudwell School and is available for all children in the school every Monday to Friday during term time. Oakwell also provides a holiday club during the school holidays and some TD days.
Breakfast Club runs from 7.30am each morning which includes breakfast and school drop off.
After-School Club runs from 3.20pm until 6pm - there are three possible booking slots (3.20-4.30pm, 3.20-5.30pm, and 3.20-6pm at variable rates, 6pm pick up is available through prior arrangement). Fresh fruit and water are available throughout and there is a light snack provided between 4pm-4.45pm. If you wish to use this club, you will need to complete a registration form. Copies of the registration form and booking forms are below.
Further details can be found on the booking form and in the terms and conditions.
For further details please contact Donna via oakwell.crudwell@gmail.com or
Holiday Club
Oakwell Holiday Club is run by Emma Waldron who studied Childcare and Education Level 3 at Cirencester college and then went onto Gloucestershire University to study Early Childhood studies (BA Hons).
Holiday club runs from 8am - 5pm. This can be extended to 5.30pm and 6pm by prior arrangement. Holiday club provides the following activities:
Snack is provided in the morning and a tuck shop is run in the afternoon (50p max per child). Lunchboxes need to be brought from home.
For more information please contact Emma via oakwell21@gmail.com.

Bookings
All bookings and payments are now made via https://oakwellchildcare.co.uk/crudwell. If you have any issues or queries please let us know directly.

Disadvantaged Learners Charter
At Crudwell Church of England Primary School, we are committed to supporting all pupils to be and do their best. We recognise that some pupils are at risk of underachievement because of the impact of socio-economic disadvantage on their learning, wellbeing and personal development.
As a school, we have signed up to the Wiltshire 'Educational Disadvantage' Charter which is an ambitious framework of best practice statements of success for these learners. Every day, in every interaction, it is in our gift to bring about the change required to overcome the challenges of disadvantage.
